wake-up.definition: To stop sleeping and become conscious of your surroundings in the morning.

get-out-of-bed.definition: To rise and leave the bed after waking up.
get-out-of-bed.exampleUsage: I get out of bed at seven on school days.

stretch.definition: To extend your arms, legs, or body to full length after waking or sitting.

brush-teeth.definition: To clean your teeth using a toothbrush and toothpaste.

wash-face.definition: To clean the face with water, usually with soap or a cleanser.
wash-face.exampleUsage: He washes his face before breakfast.

take-a-shower.definition: To wash the body while standing under running water from a shower.
take-a-shower.exampleUsage: She takes a shower after sports practice.

get-dressed.definition: To put on your clothes for the day.

eat-breakfast.definition: To have the first meal of the day, usually in the morning.
eat-breakfast.exampleUsage: We eat breakfast before leaving home.

pack-bag.definition: To put the things you need into a bag before going somewhere.
pack-bag.exampleUsage: I pack my bag the night before school.

commute.definition: To travel regularly between your home and your place of work or study.

arrive.definition: To reach a place after traveling there.

start-work.definition: To begin doing the tasks of a job or planned activity.
start-work.exampleUsage: My father starts work early in the morning.

attend-class.definition: To be present at a scheduled lesson at school or university.

take-notes.definition: To write down important points so they can be remembered or reviewed later.
take-notes.exampleUsage: Students take notes during the lesson.

have-a-meeting.definition: To meet with other people to discuss work, plans, or decisions.
have-a-meeting.exampleUsage: The team has a meeting every Monday.

lunch-break.definition: A midday pause when workers or students stop their activities to eat and rest.

collaborate.definition: To work together with others on a shared task or project.

submit-work.definition: To give completed work to a teacher, manager, or system for review.
submit-work.exampleUsage: She submits her work before the deadline.

leave-office.definition: To depart from your workplace at the end of the workday.

after-school.definition: The period of time after the school day has finished.
after-school.exampleUsage: He goes to the library after school.

homework.definition: School assignments that a student completes at home.

exercise.definition: Physical activity done regularly to improve or maintain health.

practice.definition: To do an activity or skill repeatedly in order to improve at it.

grocery-shop.definition: To buy food and everyday household items from a store or market.

cook-dinner.definition: To prepare the evening meal by cooking food.
cook-dinner.exampleUsage: They cook dinner together at home.

walk-the-dog.definition: To take a dog outside for exercise while guiding it on a leash.
walk-the-dog.exampleUsage: She walks the dog before breakfast.

play-outside.definition: To spend time playing outdoors in fresh air rather than inside a building.
play-outside.exampleUsage: The children play outside after homework.

read-a-book.definition: To look at and understand the written words in a book.
read-a-book.exampleUsage: I read a book before bedtime.

watch-tv.definition: To view programs, news, or documentaries on a television.

eat-dinner.definition: To have the main evening meal with family or friends.

wash-dishes.definition: To clean plates, cups, and cooking utensils after a meal.
wash-dishes.exampleUsage: He washes the dishes after dinner.

relax.definition: To rest quietly and enjoy a calm, peaceful feeling.

take-a-bath.definition: To wash the body in a bathtub filled with warm water.
take-a-bath.exampleUsage: The child takes a bath before bed.

put-on-pajamas.definition: To dress in comfortable clothes worn for sleeping.
put-on-pajamas.exampleUsage: She puts on pajamas after brushing her teeth.

read.definition: To look at and understand written or printed words.

set-alarm.definition: To program an alarm clock to ring at a chosen time.
set-alarm.exampleUsage: I set the alarm for six thirty.

go-to-bed.definition: To lie down in bed at night in order to sleep.

fall-asleep.definition: To stop being awake and begin sleeping.

sleep-in.definition: To stay asleep in the morning later than your usual waking time.

brunch.definition: A late morning meal eaten instead of both breakfast and lunch.

go-shopping.definition: To visit shops or markets to look for and buy needed items.
go-shopping.exampleUsage: They go shopping for school supplies on Saturday.

visit-friends.definition: To go and spend time with friends at their home or another place.
visit-friends.exampleUsage: We visit friends during the weekend.

go-to-the-park.definition: To travel to a public outdoor garden or park for fresh air and relaxation.
go-to-the-park.exampleUsage: The family goes to the park in the afternoon.

play-sports.definition: To take part in games or physical activities such as football, tennis, or basketball.
play-sports.exampleUsage: Many students play sports after school.

clean-house.definition: To tidy and clean the rooms of a home thoroughly.

do-laundry.definition: To wash, dry, and fold clothes and household linens.
do-laundry.exampleUsage: We do laundry on Friday morning.

go-out.definition: To leave your home to spend time outdoors or visit a place.

stay-home.definition: To remain at home instead of going out.
stay-home.exampleUsage: I stayed home because the weather was rainy.
